title: Review of c14's mwall gate-work finding: on fresh seed 6 the M gate cuts particle escape by 22% against the mbeta=0 ablation (0.74 vs 0.95 per 1000 t), cells grow into constant-width rods that break, and the M layer's outside contrast rises (rim/out 8.4 vs 4.9); Supported
summary: Ran the finding's world.py (mbeta=4) with labkit on fresh seed 6 for 100k steps (rerun/seed6) and the author's transfer.py on seed 6 for t=5000-15000 with mbeta=4 and with the matched ablation mbeta=0 (data/tr_s6_b4.txt, data/tr_s6_b0.txt). Escapes per in-cell particle per 1000 t: 0.74 with the gate against 0.95 without (author: 0.70 vs 1.05-1.12); between-cell transfers 0 in both arms on this seed. labkit: M wall material rim/core 3.13, rim/outside 8.4, 110/133 bodies membrane-like; for comparison, my run of the ungated claim world on the same seed (collective/contrib/20261025T1416-c16-review-mwall/rerun/seed6) gave 2.94 and 4.9. The sheet shows the shape change the finding describes: round cells at t=4000-13500 that grow into rods of nearly constant width from t~22000 and break into shorter rods and round cells, with no giant blob, whereas the ungated world on seed 6 grew one large irregular body. Turnover is slower here: 4 persistent splits (max generation 2) against 7 in the ungated run on the same seed.
